name: 39234-longdecode-gemma4e4b-1gpu
hardware: 1x H100 80GB HBM3 (one GPU of an a3 node, --gres=gpu:1).
parallelism: TP=1, PP=1, DP=1, one in-process vLLM engine.
architecture: Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration (`model_type: gemma4`), an instruction-tuned multimodal Gemma 4 checkpoint; a vision tower and an audio tower ship in the same file. Shape is read off its own config.json.
load_profile: concurrent (CLOSED loop), streams=8, warmup the first 10%, cooldown 10%, bounded at 240 requests with a 2400 s safety cap.
workload: guidellm `synthetic_text`, single turn, no prefix_buckets, TEXT ONLY -- no image and no audio input is sent. Prompt exactly 128 tokens and output exactly 1024 (min == max on both); the vllm_python backend sets ignore_eos=True whenever max_tokens is set, so every request generates exactly 1024 tokens. The backend renders the prompt into a chat message, so the engine sees a few tokens more than 128; nothing here is a function of the exact prompt length.
purpose: A long-form text generation assistant on one H100, writing 1024-token replies from short prompts for eight concurrent users.
launch:
# The engine command line for commit 79a5b6325396683d3063c41fd1a140c56c89e982
# (v0.19.1rc0-368-g79a5b63253966). Interpreter and hardware seal: configs/env.yaml.
model: google/gemma-4-E4B-it
max-model-len: 4096
tensor-parallel-size: 1
max-num-seqs: 16
max-num-batched-tokens: 2048
gpu-memory-utilization: 0.9

# OFF against the V1 default of ON, deliberately: with caching on, how much prefill a request
# performs would depend on what ran before it.
enable-prefix-caching: false
dtype: bfloat16

# `limit-mm-per-prompt` is deliberately unset. This workload sends text only, but capping a
# modality to zero changes how the engine configures the model at load time, and this setup
# serves the checkpoint exactly as a default deployment would.
